headline: Stocks grind toward fresh highs as yields ease, Fed holds
body: The tape heads into Friday's jobs report in good shape: the S&P 500 closed higher to start October as Treasury yields retreated from the multiyear highs that had weighed on risk appetite earlier in the week, and chip stocks led a Thursday comeback across the major indices. Futures were modestly higher again this morning — S&P and Dow contracts up roughly half a percent, Nasdaq-100 futures up about 0.6% — with investors looking past this week's softer inflation prints toward the September payrolls release for confirmation of the "low hire, low fire" labor backdrop. The Fed itself stayed on hold this week, keeping its benchmark rate at 3.5%–3.75% after three straight cuts late last year, with its own projections now pointing to only one more quarter-point reduction before year-end. The VIX sitting in a moderate 15–20 band captures the mood well: easing rather than euphoric, with real attention on whether the jobs data upsets the recent rally in bonds and stocks alike.

Retail positioning looks narrower than the index-level calm suggests. Chatter on Reddit's trading boards and Stocktwits is dominated by a single name — Micron — pulling in far more comment volume than Nvidia, Meta, or Microsoft combined on a firmly bullish AI-memory-demand thesis, while broader mega-cap sentiment is more mixed and Meta-related chatter has been souring. Nike is the other outlier: mentions have spiked sharply, but the tone running through that chatter is skeptical rather than celebratory, with boards debating how much further the stock could fall rather than chasing it higher. Taken together, retail enthusiasm reads as concentrated in a narrow AI-hardware pocket rather than broad risk-seeking, even as options-market positioning in SPY and QQQ stays tilted bullish ahead of the jobs number.
